- cancelling-queued-vercel-deployments: Use when queued Vercel deployments need to be cancelled by the GitHub author/login that triggered them — typically a CI bot like "actions-user" firing duplicate preview deployments, an Actions-minutes scare, or wanting a recurring sweeper to keep the queue clean while a noisy branch churns.
- deploy-to-vercel: Deploy applications and websites to Vercel. Use when the user requests deployment actions like "deploy my app", "deploy and give me the link", "push this live", or "create a preview deployment".
- effective-go: Apply Go best practices, idioms, and conventions from golang.org/doc/effective_go. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Go code to ensure idiomatic, clean, and efficient implementations.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- get-api-docs: Use this skill when you need documentation for a third-party library, SDK, or API before writing code that uses it — for example, "use the OpenAI API", "call the Stripe API", "use the Anthropic SDK", "query Pinecone", or any time the user asks you to write code against an external service and you need current API reference. Fetch the docs with chub before answering, rather than relying on training knowledge.
- merging-branches-safely: Use when asked to merge or rebase one branch into another, or when resuming an in-progress merge/rebase with unresolved conflicts. Covers `git merge`, `git rebase`, and cleanup after conflict aborts. Do not use for cherry-pick, push, or PR creation.
- rebasing-renovate-prs-locally: Use when manually rebasing a Renovate PR for a pnpm monorepo locally, instead of waiting for the Renovate workflow. Triggers on draining a Renovate PR backlog, paused Renovate cron, slow CI lockfile regeneration, or "rebase this Renovate PR now without spending Actions minutes."
- sweep-vercel-queue: Two-pass sweep of a Vercel team's QUEUED deployments. Pass 1 cancels ALL queued PREVIEW deployments by a given githubLogin (e.g. a CI bot firing a preview per project on every push). Pass 2 cancels queued PRODUCTION deployments by a given githubLogin, keeping the newest per project so the latest code still ships. Use for "sweep the Vercel queue", "drain queued previews", "cancel a bot's preview deploys", "cancel stale prod deploys keep latest per app". Both passes are opt-in via env/config.
- vercel-cli-with-tokens: Deploy and manage projects on Vercel using token-based authentication. Use when working with Vercel CLI using access tokens rather than interactive login — e.g. "deploy to vercel", "set up vercel", "add environment variables to vercel".
- vercel-composition-patterns: React composition patterns that scale. Use when refactoring components with boolean prop proliferation, building flexible component libraries, or designing reusable APIs. Triggers on tasks involving compound components, render props, context providers, or component architecture. Includes React 19 API changes.
